author: historian-agent:o-s105
title: Xhosa cattle killing
summary: In 1856 a young Xhosa woman, Nongqawuse, reported a vision promising that the ancestors would free the Xhosa from Europeans in exchange for sacrificing their wealth. Chief Sarili ordered over 150,000 cattle killed and crops destroyed, over about ten months. Freedom never came: EBSCO puts starvation deaths at about forty thousand, Gale says tens of thousands, and many survivors moved to the Cape Colony.

uncertainty.note: Gale gives the cattle sacrifice as 1856-57 and SAHO the movement as 1856-7; the span is taken from those two pages.

as_recorded.value: an action which took some ten months to complete

where.modern_name: Gxarha, near Kei Mouth, Eastern Cape, South Africa (proxy pin: OpenStreetMap place named Gxarha; the Gxarha River is where the vision is said to have occurred)
where.historical_name: Gxarha River area, Xhosaland (Gcaleka Xhosa under Sarili), beyond the Kei River from the Cape Colony

importance.justification: Gale calls the sacrifice a vision-driven destruction of Xhosa wealth followed by widespread devastation; it ended the independence of a large part of Xhosa society.

audience_note: Describes mass starvation. Death figures are estimates that differ by source.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Gxarha, Great Kei, Eastern Cape (node 262712402; -32.7051481, 28.3396802)
sources.author: OpenStreetMap contributors

reviewer_note: Death toll is given as the sources state it: about forty thousand (EBSCO Xhosa people) and "tens of thousands" (Gale); no range is computed. Pin is a proxy: the OSM suburb named Gxarha near the river mouth. No source I opened gives coordinates for the vision site, hence 25 km uncertainty. Gale and SAHO both date the movement 1856-57; SAHO notes Nongqawuse was about 15 or 16 and cites the Gxarha River.
